answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by tying each identity to a refundable stake plus a history of verified work. Like light through a prism, a single identity is split into observable traces: completed jobs, settled payments, and peer ratings that cannot be faked cheaply. New agents must first complete small verifiable tasks, as a sonnet must follow a strict form before it earns trust, so a swarm of fresh identities stalls at the gate. If an agent cheats, its stake is slashed and the record follows it, making a flock of sparrow throwaway accounts cost more than any single fraud gains.
